target_customer: Fast growing consumer brands that need working capital tied up in inventory
problem: Consumer brands pay suppliers up front for inventory and wait months to be paid by sales, which locks up cash.
business_model: Supply chain finance: pays supplier invoices up front and charges brands a fee when they repay after inventory sells
product_category: Supply chain finance for consumer brands

founders.name: Rob LaFave
previous_startups: Foodzie.com (online marketplace for artisan foodcrafters, sold)
founders.background_notes: YC page calls him a technologist, entrepreneur, investor and urban farmer; Foodzie was named by Fast Company among Most Innovative Food Companies. A search snippet attributes the Foodzie sale to Joyus in 2012, rests on CB Insights.

competitors.name: Settle
competitors.what: Pays vendors for e-commerce brands up front and gets repaid when the brand turns the inventory into revenue

technical_complexity.rationale: Underwriting and payment workflow software with a two person team; the hard part is credit risk and capital sourcing, not engineering.

defensibility.rationale: Lending products are copyable and depend on access to capital; no proprietary data or lock in was found for a two person team.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Better funded inventory financiers kept serving consumer brands; no outcome for Float was found.

market_need_then: DTC and consumer brands in 2021 needed inventory cash and revenue based financiers were raising large rounds; no Float specific demand evidence found.

branding.domain_note: float.xyz now redirects to a GoDaddy for sale page (seen at research time), suggesting the domain was dropped or parked.

identity.voice_and_tone: Tagline framed as Pipe for supply chain finance

brand_strength.rationale: The name is shared by several unrelated Float fintechs (Float Financial Canada, gofloat.io, others) and no press or brand assets were found.

outcome_analysis: Float is listed as active with two people in Honolulu, but its float.xyz website now redirects to a domain for sale page and no funding, product news or exit was found. The outcome is therefore unclear; it may have stalled or changed name. Competitors such as Settle had raised venture funding by mid 2021.
notes: A CB Insights profile (unverified, may be another company) shows a 130K seed from Y Combinator on 2021-09-01; not recorded as a round. Other companies named Float (SVB 50M financing, Float Financial Canada, EUR4.5M Series A) are unrelated. YC page lists only Rob LaFave as founder; a theorg listing calls him co-founder but names no other. No outcome news found. Update: the $130K seed from Y Combinator dated 2021-09-01 rests on a single database (CB Insights) and is now recorded; Crunchbase shows only a pre-seed raise without a matching amount.
